chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the hunting of fish, even if they are not named (specific species), he said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat fish caught without specifying the species?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the general permissibility of consuming fish caught through hunting, even without specifying the species, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that aquatic creatures are inherently pure and lawful unless explicitly prohibited. It underscores the simplicity of the ruling in contrast to the more complex conditions required for land animals, highlighting the ease granted in dietary laws regarding sea harvest.
